atoms.text: The ancient Maya were an advanced civilisation that originated in Mesoamerica, an area that spreads across modern Central America.
Developing from small settlements in around 2000 BC, the Maya built a network of independent “city-states”, strongly connected through their trade and shared religious beliefs.

hint.text: This map shows the modern-day countries and borders, but they did not exist back then!

atoms.text: Today, the Maya are admired for their cultural and technical achievements, such as their impressive pyramids, complex writing system and solar calendars.

atoms.a: Which area did the Maya civilisation spread across?

atoms.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

atoms.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

instruction.text: Match the different climates of Mesoamerica to the correct labels.

feedback.finish: The Maya had to adapt to a variety of climates. This was especially true in the Yucatán Peninsular, which had wet and dry seasons with both heavy, tropical rains and also droughts.

instruction.text: Find and select Chichen Itza to learn more about Maya civilisation.
instruction.sound: Find and select Chitchen Itza to learn more about Maya civilisation.

feedback.finish: Chichen Itza, in the region of Yucatán, was the most powerful Maya city-state. It was a centre of trade and is considered sacred by the Maya.

atoms.b: The Maya city-states were well-connected through a series of ((++roads airports)), so they could trade goods like cacao beans, fruits and maize.
atoms.sound: The Maya city-states were well-connected through a series of roads, so they could trade goods like kacow beans, fruits and maize.

atoms.b: Most of the city-states had similar features, like ((++markets cinemas)), temples and ball courts.
Despite their trade links and similar features, the Maya city-states still differed from one other. They each had their own ((++leaders readers)) and unique ((++architecture chairs)).

instruction.text: Select the mixture inside the bowl to find out about Maya culture today.

feedback.finish: Despite the decline of the ancient civilisation, there are still over 7 million Maya living today. They have preserved their culture by speaking Mayan languages, cooking traditional food and performing ancient Maya rituals.
